chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ya'qub al-Ahmar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever swears an oath while he knows that he is a liar has indeed challenged God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.بَارَزَ: Challenged/dueled; from the root b-r-z meaning to step forward in confrontation — implies open, brazen opposition
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; divine epithet emphasising God's absolute power and transcendence, highlighting the enormity of challenging Him
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath/sworn statement; in Islamic jurisprudence, a yamin is a binding declaration made in God's name

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about swearing a false oath?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a severe warning against false oaths (al-yamin al-ghamus), declaring that knowingly swearing a false oath is an act of open defiance and confrontation against God Himself. The Arabic term 'baraza' (بَارَزَ) carries the image of a soldier who steps forward on the battlefield to challenge an opponent to single combat — an act of extreme audacity when directed at the Divine. This teaching was addressed to a community familiar with tribal oaths as bonds of honour and social contract, making the gravity of violating that sanctity with conscious falsehood particularly stark.
